newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Hun Sen claims no coup, says prince can return.
newsitem.headline: Hun Sen claims no coup, says prince can return.

text.p: Cambodia's strongman Hun Sen on Thursday denied bloody fighting at the weekend was a coup, and said his ousted co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh could return to the country and face legal proceedings.

Hun Sen also warned against foreign interference in Cambodia, as the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) said it still recognised Ranariddh as Cambodia's co-premier and postponed Cambodia's membership into the regional group.

Hun Sen made the comments to reporters just days after ousting Ranariddh as First Prime Minister and taking control of Phnom Penh during clashes over the weekend. The prince had left Cambodia for France on the eve of the fighting.
The clashes left at least 58 people dead and up to 200 wounded.

"It is not a coup d'etat. If I made a coup d'etat I would change the monarchy to a republic, suspend the constitution and arrest FUNCINPEC ministers, but everything is still the same," Hun Sen said, referring to Ranariddh's royalist party.
"I did not expel Ranariddh. Ranariddh fled by himself," he said. "I will not invite him to return but I will not ban him from coming back. Ranariddh can come back to face court."
He did not say what sort of proceedings Ranariddh would face but has said previously the prince should be put on trial for illegally negotiating with the Khmer Rouge guerrillas.
After the weekend violence, Ranariddh accused Hun Sen of staging a coup. He said later he would form a resistance.
Hun Sen also said the international community should stay out of Cambodia's affairs.
"I cannot please foreigners all the time, but I have to please my own people. I urge all foreigners to be cautious with what they are going to decide for Cambodia," Hun Sen said.
Hun Sen also accused Ranariddh of provoking his own overthrow through a "reckless strategy of provocation".

The foreign ministry said in a white paper that Ranariddh had destabilised Cambodia by openly criticising Hun Sen's political party, building up his armed forces and weapons stocks, conducting secret negotiations with Khmer Rouge rebels and forming a political alliance that included the Khmer Rouge.
The Cambodian capital was tense on Thursday as foreigners scrambled to leave and supporters of Ranariddh's party were either fleeing or falling in line with the new regime.

Cambodia's ambassador to the United Nations, a Ranariddh loyalist, said on Wednesday in New York that the prince's forces would capture Battambang, the country's second largest city, and set up an alternative government there.

But Thai army and Khmer Rouge guerrilla sources said on Thursday that royalist forces had agreed a ceasefire with Hun Sen's troops in western Cambodia after failing to enlist the support of ex-Khmer Rouge remnants in the area.

A military official loyal to Hun Sen told Reuters from the town on Thursday the situation there was quiet, while in Phnom Penh the government said it would fly diplomats and journalists to Battambang and Siem Reap so they could assess the situation.
Nervous FUNCINPEC party officials continued leaving the country on Thursday in the aftermath of the arrest and execution of a senior party member on Monday.
Ho Sok, a secretary of state in the interior ministry, was arrested by Hun Sen's troops on Monday and later shot dead, government officials said.

Hun Sen had earlier blamed Ho Sok and three other senior FUNCINPEC members for the weekend's fighting and said they all had to be hunted down and arrested. A FUNCINPEC intelligence officer, Chao Sambath, was among the four. There were unconfirmed reports that he had also been arrested and killed, and a newspaper which supports Hun Sen reported on Thursday that he had committed suicide.
The same newspaper reported that Ho Sok had killed himself though officials later said he had been shot dead by soldiers.

But while some royalists fled the country, others were cooperating with the new regime. Several prominent FUNCINPEC officials, including at least two ministers, attended Hun Sen's first cabinet meeting as sole prime minister on Thursday.
Hun Sen said earlier he wanted FUNCINPEC to nominate a new person to fill Ranariddh's job as First Prime Minister.
The United States plans to pull out about 40 diplomats and their dependants and also urged all Americans to leave. Between 1,000 and 1,300 Americans are in Cambodia, a U.S. official said.
Anxious foreigners jammed information desks at hotels and airline offices in the city on Thursday, demanding seats on heavily-booked commercial and charter flights out of the city.
Cambodia's Southeast Asian neighbours continued evacuating their nationals on Thursday and Australia said it also would evacuate its citizens.
